title: Entropy threshold: A simple proxy for performance of quantum error correction
abstract: The rapidly growing landscape of quantum error-correction (QEC) protocols has produced a wealth of numerical data, but comparatively few heuristics for understanding and predicting their performance. Here, we develop a simple entropy-based proxy that predicts the thresholds of a variety of QEC protocols, ranging from the code-capacity setting of Clifford-deformed surface codes with biased Pauli or erasure noise to the circuit-level noise model of the surface or color codes with flag qubits. Our proxy estimates the threshold by locally comparing the noise entropy with the error information gained via stabilizer measurements (or spacetime detectors and flag outcomes in the circuit-level settings). Despite neglecting correlations between stabilizer outcomes and the contribution from code degeneracy, the proxy captures the main trends across diverse settings and yields threshold estimates in good agreement with numerical results. Our work develops much-needed phenomenology that enables simple back-of-the-envelope estimates of QEC performance, recovering and providing an explanation for the results of computationally intensive detailed simulations.
summary: This work introduces an entropy-based heuristic to predict the performance threshold of quantum error correction codes. By comparing the entropy generated by physical noise against the information extracted via syndrome measurements, the authors provide a simple, generalizable tool. This method successfully predicts thresholds across diverse code types and noise models, offering significant phenomenological insight into QEC performance.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop simple, predictive heuristics for determining the performance threshold of various Quantum Error Correction (QEC) protocols, circumventing the intractability of exact analytical calculations.
main_result: An entropy-based proxy successfully captures the main trends across diverse QEC settings, yielding threshold estimates in good agreement with computationally intensive numerical simulations.
method: The core method involves developing an entropy decomposition that locally compares the noise entropy (from physical errors) with the syndrome entropy (information gained from stabilizer measurements).
model_or_system: The analysis applies to various QEC codes, including Clifford-deformed surface codes (XY, XZZX) and color codes, tested under different noise models such as biased Pauli noise, erasure noise, and circuit-level noise.
key_observables: Threshold ($p_{th}$), Noise Entropy ($H(E)$), Syndrome Entropy ($H(S)$), and Logical Error Rate ($p_L$).
important_parameters: Physical error rate ($p$), noise bias ($\eta$), and code size ($n$).
main_assumptions: The proxy neglects correlations between stabilizer outcomes and the contribution from code degeneracy, and for soft information, it relies on modeling measurement outcomes with Gaussian distributions.
figures_summary: Figures compare the entropy threshold lines derived from the proxy against numerical results for surface and color codes under various noise conditions (e.g., Fig. 1 and Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the entropy-based proxy by deriving bounds on the logical error rate using conditional entropy, then applies this heuristic to various code types and noise models, culminating in discussions on incorporating soft information.
why_interesting: The development of simple, generalizable heuristics that match complex simulation results provides powerful, 'back-of-the-envelope' tools for assessing QEC feasibility without running massive simulations.
